To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two kinds of algorithms are proposed for computing attribute-value block in incomplete decision systems, which are far more efficient when dealing with "don't care" conditions and are relatively insensitive to missing values.

the proposed algorithms can efficiently compute attribute-value blocks for both "do not cares" conditions and "missing values", and the proposed algorithms constitute an effective solution for efficiently computing attribute-value block for incomplete decision systems.
the proposed algorithms, especially the index algorithm, are efficient methods of computing the attribute-value blocks for both CRRMSs and TRRMSs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of efficient algorithms for attribute-value blocks in the context of rough set theory.
the construction of efficient and practical methods of computing attributevalue blocks, which is of great significance to the applications of rough set theory.

the efficient computation of attribute-value blocks in rough set models, which can provide a theoretical basis for the efficient computation of other rough set operations, such as attribute reductions, rule reductions, etc.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed algorithms can be used to efficiently compute attribute-value blocks for all incomplete decision systems, which are the most frequently used and basic operations for almost all computations in rough set models.
the proposed methods constitute a very effective and efficient method to deal with incomplete decision systems, especially when dealing with "lost values".
the index algorithm is more efficient than the usual methods when missing values are relatively large, while the division algorithm is more efficient when missing values are small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed methods are efficient for incomplete decision systems containing only "do no care" conditions, and relatively efficient for incomplete decision system containing both "do no care conditions" and "lost values".
the proposed algorithms can be applied to the efficient construction of attribute reduction and other computations based on attribute-value block for incomplete decision systems.
the two proposed methods can be used as the basis to develop more efficient algorithms for other computations, such as rule reduction and so on.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when missing values exist in a decision system, it is not a wise choice to compute attribute-value blocks in the way of computing them for complete decision systems.
we have proposed efficient algorithms for computing attribute-value block for incomplete decision systems.

the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the computational time of computing attribute-value sets for incomplete decision systems, which is of great significance to improve the efficiency of rough set models.
